summary.intent: Continue a series of CI/release hardening PRs in the callisto repo: finish the action-pin PR (#448), then tighten the fake `cargo publish` in the release e2e harness so it requires `--registry` for custom registries, and ensure a test actually guards that behavior.
summary.outcome: PR #448 was retitled/updated. A stricter fake cargo publish was added to the release harness, and since a mutation check showed no e2e test exercised custom registries, a provider-level unit test (`a_cargo_publish_names...`) was added that fails when the registry flag is dropped. Both were committed and pushed on `test/fake-cargo-publish-requires-registry`; clippy was run.

repo: Release e2e suites live in crates/callisto-cli/tests (durable_release_e2e, release_command_e2e, release_forge_publish_e2e, release_hardening, provider_flag_contract, stageable_targets_e2e, shallow_clone_e2e, nested_cargo_workspace_e2e); 105 tests passed with the stricter fake.
No e2e fixture configures a custom cargo registry, so e2e tests cannot detect a dropped `--registry` flag on publish.
Provider tests in callisto-graph's registry/tests.rs already have a RecordingRunner and an `operation` helper, making them the right place to assert argv for a custom registry key.
Production argv is built in callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs (`cargo_publish_argv`), and the provider passes `registry_key` at cargo.rs:103.
The 'Released N package(s)' summary overclaiming on reruns is a known pending fix (OperationOutcome / ReleaseReceiptV1 in callisto-model/src/release).

code.finding: The publish call passes `registry_key`; replacing it with `None` is the mutation that the new provider-level test catches.
`cargo_publish_argv` appends `--registry` only when `registry_key` is Some; forcing the filter to false did not fail any e2e test, revealing the coverage gap.

workflow: Run a mutation check (temporarily break production code) after tightening a test fake to confirm the test actually discriminates; here it exposed a guard that guarded nothing.
Revert mutations with `git checkout -- <file>` and re-run the test to confirm restoration.
Work is being done in a worktree with each fix on its own branch off origin/main (`--no-track`), one PR per concern.

friction: The initial mutation (dropping `--registry` from production argv) survived all 105 e2e tests, so the stricter fake alone provided no protection and required a different test layer.
Started a branch for the release-summary fix, then deleted it and switched away to do the fake-cargo work first, leaving that task unstarted.
open_items: Fix the 'Released N package(s)' summary so it counts only actually published packages rather than overclaiming on reruns (branch fix/release-summary-counts-published was created and discarded without changes).
No e2e fixture exercises a custom cargo registry; consider adding one so the stricter fake guards real end-to-end behavior.
PR for test/fake-cargo-publish-requires-registry was pushed with a body drafted in pr-cargo-registry.md but the PR itself was not shown as opened; clippy result was not displayed.
